headline: A store clerk stops a runaway school bus

sources.title: St. Paul hero receives $1K award for saving kids, driver on runaway school bus (MPR News)
Video shows quick-thinking bystander stop runaway St. Paul school bus (CBS Minnesota)
27-year-old man credited for saving kids, driver in runaway school bus (ABC News)

chunks.text: On October 19, 2026, a 27-year-old store clerk in St. Paul, Minnesota, was kicking a soccer ball outside his family's [[corner store]]. Business was slow that afternoon. He {{grew up}} in the city. A school bus had just {{dropped off}} some children nearby. Then it rolled slowly past the store with its door [[wide open]]. The clerk looked inside and saw that the driver was having a [[medical emergency]].

verbs.wrong: To find a first job in a city
verbs.why: Children who grow up on farms learn to work hard. Many kids grow up near their grandparents. The clerk grew up in the city where he works at his family's store.

verbs.correct: To leave someone at a place
verbs.wrong: To count children on a bus
verbs.why: Parents drop off their kids at school every morning. The city bus drops me off near my house. A school bus had just dropped off some children near the store.

chunks.text: The clerk [[sprinted]] to the bus and jumped [[aboard]]. He had never driven a bus before. He tried to put it in park, but it went into reverse [[by mistake]]. He {{ended up}} putting it in neutral and pulling the [[parking brake]]. He gave a girl at the front his phone and glasses to {{hold on to}}. A student called the police, and officers {{pulled up}} within minutes.

verbs.correct: To finally do something after trying
verbs.wrong: To ask someone how to do something
verbs.why: I look at three shirts and end up buying the blue one. She tries many keys and ends up using the last one. After the bus went into reverse, the clerk ended up putting it in neutral.

verbs.correct: To keep something safe for someone
verbs.wrong: To take a photo of something
verbs.why: My friend holds on to my keys when I swim. The teacher holds on to our phones during a test. The clerk gave a girl his phone and glasses to hold on to.

verbs.correct: To arrive and stop in a vehicle
verbs.wrong: To use the lights and the siren
verbs.why: A taxi pulls up in front of the hotel. My dad pulls up at the school gate at three. After a student called the police, officers pulled up within minutes.

chunks.text: No one was hurt. [[Paramedics]] took the driver to the hospital. The [[school district]] said on October 21 that the driver was resting at home. The district says 19 middle school students were on the bus. Another bus came to {{pick them up}} and take them home. The next day, the school's [[mental health]] team {{checked in with}} students. The store's [[security video]] shows him running to the bus, which {{backs up}} his story. He says he was scared at first that police might [[arrest]] him.

verbs.correct: To collect someone in a vehicle
verbs.wrong: To check someone's name on a list
verbs.why: My mom picks me up after soccer practice. The airport bus picks up travelers at every hotel. Another bus came to pick the students up and take them home.

verbs.correct: To talk to someone to see if they are okay
verbs.wrong: To write a report about each student
verbs.why: Nurses check in with patients every few hours. I check in with my grandmother by phone each night. The school's mental health team checked in with students the next day.

verbs.correct: To show that something is true
verbs.wrong: To make something hard to see
verbs.why: The numbers back up her idea. Photos back up his story about the storm. The store's security video backs up the clerk's story.

chunks.text: On October 22, a local [[media personality]] surprised the clerk at the store. She brought a man dressed as Superman and {{handed over}} a [[giant]] check for 1,000 dollars. She said he {{stepped in}} like a [[real-life]] [[superhero]]. The clerk plans to use the money for his own small business. He {{plays down}} his [[bravery]]. He says he felt it was his [[duty]], and that anyone would have done the same.

verbs.wrong: To sign your name on a check
verbs.why: The waiter hands over the bill at the end of the meal. Drivers hand over their tickets at the gate. A local media personality handed over a giant check for 1,000 dollars.

verbs.correct: To get involved to help in a problem
verbs.wrong: To act in a superhero movie
verbs.why: A teacher steps in when two kids start to fight. Neighbors often step in when an old man needs help. A local media personality said the clerk stepped in like a real-life superhero.

verbs.correct: To say something is less important
verbs.wrong: To tell a story many times
verbs.why: My dad plays down his health problems. Good leaders do not play down bad news. The clerk plays down his bravery and says anyone would do the same.

mainIdea.s: A store clerk in St. Paul stopped a rolling school bus after its driver had a medical emergency. No children were hurt, and a local woman later gave him a reward of 1,000 dollars.
mainIdea.why: The clerk stepped in when the driver had a medical emergency. A local media personality later handed over a giant check to thank him.

mainIdea.s: A young St. Paul man jumped onto a school bus whose brakes had suddenly stopped working. The city's school district then thanked him with a cash prize at his family's shop.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the driver had a medical emergency, not broken brakes. The reward came from a local media personality, not the school district.

mainIdea.s: Minnesota schools are hiring more bus drivers after many bus routes ran late in September. Officials say each new driver will get extra safety training before carrying any students.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a clerk who stopped a rolling school bus. Another bus came to pick the students up, and no one was hurt.

tf.s: A store clerk stepped in when a school bus driver had a medical emergency.
tf.why: He saw the driver was in trouble, sprinted to the bus and stopped it.

tf.s: Several children on the bus were badly hurt.
tf.why: No one was hurt. Another bus came to pick the students up and take them home.

tf.s: The clerk had driven many buses before that day.
tf.why: He had never driven a bus before, but he still stepped in to stop it.

tf.s: The clerk ended up putting the bus in neutral to stop it.
tf.why: It went into reverse first. Then he ended up putting it in neutral and pulling the parking brake.

tf.s: A man dressed as Superman came to the store to help thank the clerk.
tf.why: He came with a local media personality, who handed over a check for 1,000 dollars.

tf.s: The clerk says he did not feel any duty to help.
tf.why: He says he felt it was his duty. He also plays down his bravery and says anyone would do the same.

lines.text: Did you see the video of that school bus in St. Paul?
The bus had just {{dropped off}} some kids, and then it kept rolling with the door open. The driver was having a medical emergency.
Oh no. That sounds like [[a close call]].
It was. A store clerk saw it and {{stepped in}}. He jumped aboard and stopped the bus.
Did he know how to drive a bus?
Not at all. It went into reverse first, but he {{ended up}} putting it in neutral.
Wow. In a moment like that, you have to [[think on your feet]].
He even gave his phone and glasses to a girl to {{hold on to}}.
No. The police {{pulled up}} in minutes, and another bus came to {{pick the kids up}}. The driver went home to rest later.
Thank goodness. He was [[in the right place at the right time]].
Then on October 22, a local media personality surprised him at his store with a man dressed as Superman. She {{handed over}} a big check.
That's so sweet. Stories like this [[restore my faith in humanity]].
The funny part is that he {{plays down}} what he did. He says anyone would do the same.
Maybe. He did it [[in a heartbeat]], but I'm not sure I would.
Same here. And the store's video {{backs up}} everything he says.

expressions.def: To make good decisions quickly, with no time to plan

expressions.expr: in the right place at the right time
expressions.def: Used when someone is lucky to be where they are needed

expressions.def: Used when a kind act makes you believe that people are good
ex: A stranger paid for my coffee. It helped restore my faith in humanity.

expressions.def: Very quickly and without stopping to think
ex: If they offered me that job, I would take it in a heartbeat.
